ud5.4:0.2: The Discourse about the Young Boys
ud5.4:1.2: at one time the Fortunate One was dwelling near Sāvatthī, in Jeta’s Wood, at Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
ud5.4:1.3: Then at that time many young boys who were between Sāvatthī and Jeta’s Wood were catching little fish.
ud5.4:2.1: Then the Fortunate One, having dressed in the morning time, after picking up his bowl and robe, was entering Sāvatthī for alms.
ud5.4:2.2: The Fortunate One saw those many young boys who were between Sāvatthī and Jeta’s Wood catching fish.
ud5.4:2.3: Having seen (that), he went to those young boys, and after going, he said this to those young boys:
ud5.4:2.4: “Are you afraid, boys, of suffering? Is suffering unpleasant to you?”
ud5.4:2.5: “Yes, reverend Sir, we are afraid of suffering, suffering is unpleasant to us.”
ud5.4:3.1: Then the Fortunate One, having understood the significance of it, on that occasion uttered this exalted utterance:
ud5.4:4.2: ~ if suffering is unpleasant to you,
ud5.4:4.4: ~ whether in the open or in secret.
ud5.4:5.1: But if you will do, or (now) do do bad deeds,
ud5.4:5.3: For you there is no freedom from suffering,
ud5.4:5.4: ~ even after going, while running away.”
